title: Loops That Stop Safely
goal: This lesson covers how to keep while loops finite by always updating the counter so the condition can become False.
learn: Spot a loop that would never stop
Always change the value the condition checks
Prefer a clear counter update every pass
idea: A while loop that never changes its condition runs forever, and that can freeze your program. The safe rule is that whatever the condition looks at (like count), something inside the loop has to change it. Shrinking, growing, or stepping a counter is the usual fix. In this course we only write finite while loops with counters, so no loops that wait forever.

lines: # Another safe pattern: grow past the limit

changeOneLine: In the editor above, change the first count = 3 to count = 2 and press Run. You should see Tick 2, Tick 1, then Stopped safely.

lines: # This would be unsafe if we forgot to update:
# while x > 0: print(x)   # x never changes!

practice.text: Fix the loop so it stops. Print count each time and subtract 1 until count is no longer greater than 0.
practice.hint: The while keeps going while count > 0. You have to change count inside the loop or it will never end.
practice.starterTip: On the blank line under the comment, try count = count - 1. You should print 4, 3, 2, 1, then Safe stop.
practice.starter:
count = 4
while count > 0:
    print(count)
    # Update count so the loop can end
    
print("Safe stop")
practice.gradingNote: Pass if while prints 4..1, count decreases each pass, then Safe stop. Infinite loops fail.

practice.text: Start steps at 0. While steps is less than 5, print steps and add 1. Print Finished after the loop.
practice.hint: steps starts at 0. Each pass should print the current steps, then bump steps up by 1 before the while checks again.
practice.starterTip: Fill the blank with steps = steps + 1 (inside the while). Output should be 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, then Finished.
practice.gradingNote: Pass if 0..4 print, steps increases, and Finished prints after. Finite while only.

quiz.question: What is wrong with: x = 5 then while x > 0: print(x) with no other lines?

options.text: Nothing. It prints 5 once and stops
It runs forever because x never changes
It prints nothing because 5 > 0 is False

quiz.correct: Right, x never changes, so x > 0 stays True forever.
quiz.wrong: If the condition never becomes False, the while loop never stops.

quiz.question: What is one safe habit for while loops in this course?

options.text: Always update a counter so the loop can end

quiz.correct: Yes, a changing counter keeps the loop finite.
quiz.wrong: Update the value your condition checks on every pass.

quiz.question: Why are infinite loops a problem?

options.text: They can freeze the program so later code never runs
They only happen with for loops

quiz.correct: Right, a loop that never ends blocks the rest of your program.
quiz.wrong: If the while never stops, the lines after it never get to run.

project.title: Safe Timer
project.desc: Start seconds at 5. While seconds > 0, print the seconds left and then subtract 1. After the loop, print Time is up! Make sure the counter always updates.
project.starter:
seconds = 5
while seconds > 0:
    print("Seconds left:", seconds)
    # Subtract 1. Required for a safe stop
    
print("Time is up!")
